title: Computing Eigenvalues
description: Gershgorin discs, power method, inverse iteration, Rayleigh quotient, QR algorithm.
html:
🔍 Computing Eigenvalues

1. Gershgorin

$$K_i = \{z : |z - a_{ii}| \le \textstyle\sum_{j\ne i}|a_{ij}|\}, \qquad \sigma(A) \subseteq \bigcup_i K_i$$

Also for columns; $0\notin\bigcup K_i$ ⇒ invertible; $\rho(A) \le \max_i(|a_{ii}| + r_i)$. The characteristic polynomial is useless for large matrices.

2. Power Method and Rayleigh Quotient

$$v_{k+1} = \frac{Av_k}{\|Av_k\|}, \qquad \lambda_1 \approx R(v_k) = \frac{v_k^TAv_k}{v_k^Tv_k}, \qquad \text{rate } \Bigl|\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}\Bigr|$$

Example $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}$, $v_0 = (1,1)$

Rayleigh: $3.5,\ 3.6,\ 3.6154,\ 3.6176 \to \lambda_1 = \frac{5+\sqrt5}{2} = 3.618034$; rate $0.382$. Rayleigh error quadratic in the vector error (symmetric).

Required: dominant eigenvalue, $c_1 \ne 0$, normalisation in every step.

3. Inverse Iteration and Shift

$$(A - \mu I)x_{k+1} = v_k \;\Rightarrow\; \text{eigenvalue near } \mu \ (\text{rate } \tfrac{|\lambda - \mu|}{|\lambda' - \mu|})$$

$\mu = 0$: smallest eigenvalue. Rayleigh quotient iteration ($\mu_k = R(v_k)$): cubic.

4. QR Algorithm

$$A_k = Q_kR_k, \quad A_{k+1} = R_kQ_k = Q_k^TA_kQ_k$$

Similar ⇒ same eigenvalues; diagonal → eigenvalues. Example: $\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\ \begin{pmatrix}3.5&0.5\\0.5&1.5\end{pmatrix},\ \begin{pmatrix}3.6&0.2\\0.2&1.4\end{pmatrix}$. In practice: Hessenberg form, shifts, deflation.

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Power method without normalisation (overflow).
  • Rayleigh quotient without the denominator $v^Tv$.
  • Applying the power method for $|\lambda_1| = |\lambda_2|$.
